text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - A two-day UK share rally ran out of steam on Tuesday as a weak Wall Street and continued worries about possible interest rate hikes, pushed prices marginally lower. The FTSE 100 index of leading shares closed 2.4 points down to 4,269.3.

FRANKFURT - German shares were off the day's highs and below the high levels seen late on Monday in afternoon trading, as the market took a pause for breath after surging three percent yesterday. The DAX index ended up points 16.88 at 3,329.76. In post-bourse trade the index fell 14.64 to 3,328.13.

PARIS - French shares, drawing support from dollar strength, limped to a higher close. But traders said the market lacked volume to make a convincing advance. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 6.69 points or 0.26 percent at 2,579.

ZURICH - Swiss shares recovered from early weakness to end little changed in quiet trade after Monday's 2.6 percent jump. Dealers said insecurity about further developments on Wall Street kept a lid on shares. They said that directionless trade may last until Friday, when U.S. economic data are due. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) closed 4.19 points lower at 2,898.96.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended Tuesday's session with sharp gains after export-strong shares rallied, inspired by the yen's weakness against the dollar, brokers said. But they said sectors burdened by bad loans were still weak. The 225-share Nikkei average rose 306.03 points or 1.73 percent to end at 18,021.70.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed higher on Tuesday, helped by interest in HSBC Holdings, while trading volumes appeared to be slowly increasing. The Hang Seng Index finished up 110.73 points or 0.90 percent at 12,398.57.

SYDNEY - A sleepy Australian share market ended a dull day barely higher on Tuesday with hesitant investors reluctant to commit funds to a drifting market. The All Ordinaries index added 2.9 points to close at 2,368.9.

JOHANNESBURG - South African industrial stocks ended near the day's weakest levels after slow drift down on profit-taking and futures arbitrage activity. Golds stayed just firm as bullion bounced around the $349 level. Industrial index ended down 40.9 points at 8,244.7. The gold index added 9.8 points to 1,327.8 and the overall index fell 30.6 to 7,044.1.
